fm.title: Firearms Training Mechanics
fm.description: Fenrith’s brutal firearms training mini-game, “The Black Powder Crucible,” turns reckless shooters into disciplined gunners through a three-phase series of skill challenges that test speed, precision, and composure under fire.
fm.overview: Fenrith doesn’t train amateurs—he breaks them down and rebuilds them into disciplined gunners. His regimen focuses on speed, precision, and unflinching nerve under live-fire conditions. The training sequence consists of three escalating phases, followed by a final integrated test.

phases.name: Loading Under Fire (Speed & Stress)
phases.goal: Successfully load and fire a musket or flintlock pistol before an advancing enemy reaches you.
mechanics: Firearms have a loading time requiring a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check.
The enemy advances each round while the shooter attempts to reload before melee range.

modifiers: +2 DC if under duress (enemy within 10 feet).

process: Each round, roll Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) to reload.
Failure: The enemy closes distance; retry next round.
Success: Weapon is loaded; shooter can fire next turn.
failure_consequences: If enemy reaches melee before firing, shooter must either:
• Strength Check (DC 15) to push them back.
• Draw a melee weapon (losing next turn).
trainee_perks: Advantage when using pre-measured powder charges.

phases.name: The Iron Eye (Marksmanship & Control)
phases.goal: Hit three moving targets at different distances before time runs out.
mechanics: Shooters make attack rolls against three targets at varying distances.
Each target has an AC based on distance and movement.
Shooter may choose between careful aiming (bonus to hit) or quick firing (reload speed).

modifiers: -5 unless spending a full round aiming.

process: Shooter picks a target and fires.
Roll attack using Dexterity + Proficiency with firearms.
On hit: advance to next target.
On miss: choose to re-aim (lose a round, +3 bonus) or fire immediately (no bonus).
trainee_perks: Advantage on one firearm attack per long rest.

phases.name: Firearms Are Liars (Misfires & Malfunctions)
phases.goal: Learn to manage gun malfunctions without panicking.
mechanics: Each shot has a chance to misfire, especially in poor conditions or under stress.
On misfire, the shooter must fix the weapon before firing again.

misfire_table.fix: Action: DC 15 Tinker’s Tools or Strength check.
Bonus Action: DC 12 Tinker’s Tools or Strength check.

process: On a natural 1 (or 2 for muskets), the weapon misfires.
Roll Dexterity (Tinker’s Tools) or Strength to clear jam.
Failure: weapon remains jammed until next turn.
Critical failure: firearm disabled for remainder of fight.
weather_modifiers: Heavy Rain: misfires on 1–3 instead of 1–2.
Humid Jungle Conditions: misfires on 1–4 unless powder properly stored.
trainee_perks: Once per day, may automatically clear a misfire as a free action.

final_test.name: The Gauntlet (Combined Trial)
final_test.goal: Fire three shots at moving targets while under fire, avoiding misfires and completing the drill before the enemy reaches the trainee.
sequence: Roll to load → success allows firing; failure lets enemy advance.
Roll to hit → choose careful or fast shooting.
Roll for misfire → fix or adapt.

scoring.perfect: 3/3 hits, no misfires, never reached by enemy.
scoring.failure: No hits, jammed gun, or tackled before firing.

trainee_perks: Fenrith’s Drills: once per long rest, reload instantly (no roll required).
Nerves of Steel: on misfire, may still take another action.

fm.flavor_text: “Firearms ain't for the weak-hearted. The musket don’t care if you’re scared. The pistol don’t care if you’re slow. You get one shot—make it count. Or someone else will.” — Fenrith

# Event Threat Level

## Event-Based Stealth Rolls
Characters roll Stealth when:
- Moving through predator territory or enemy camps.  
- Passing through noisy terrain (mud, streams, leaves).  
- Climbing/descending obstacles (trees, ruins).  
- Interacting with dense foliage/objects.  
- Killing an enemy where others may hear.

fm.title: Phased Threat Escalation
fm.description: A phased threat-progression framework for The Deep Green campaign arc. Each phase represents an escalation of danger, corruption, and environmental influence as the party approaches Vexir and the Hollow Song Temple.

phases.name: Wild Jungle (Outer Hexes)
encounters: Forgotten shrines to Sedna and false gods
Warnings carved in druidic or abyssal script
phases.effect: Threats feel indifferent but deadly—nature is not yet aware of the intruders.

phases.name: The Encroached Zone (Mid-Jungle)
phases.mood: Wrongness seeps into the air—rot without flies, trees without birds, stone with veins.
phases.trigger: Once within three hexes of Vexir.
effects: Normal jungle encounters shift to include cult influence and residual magic.
All Perception and Insight checks are made with disadvantage unless a light source is carried.
Pinch’s map tools start to draw symbols on their own during long rests.
encounters: Disfigured animals with extra eyes or fused limbs.
Unborn scouts hiding in trees (silent observers).
Cult totems made from knotted hair and bone.
A ruined camp of explorers who worshiped the Pretender after succumbing to madness.
Possessed beasts that act with synchronized, intelligent aggression.
phases.effect: The party begins to feel watched. Rest becomes less effective. Divine casters may experience ominous dreams or blocked guidance.

phases.name: The Hollow Grove (Temple Perimeter)
phases.mood: Sacrilege made manifest—the jungle is not dead, it’s listening.
phases.trigger: Last one to two hexes surrounding Vexir.
terrain_changes: Twisted trees grow in impossible shapes, leaning toward the mountain.
Air is thick with droning, like a song beneath the threshold of hearing.
Sound is muffled—speech echoes wrong, music distorts.
The sun never fully penetrates the canopy, even at noon.
mechanics: Stealth is nearly impossible due to muttering roots and noise-warping flora.
Spellcasting within this zone risks wild effects (DM may roll or apply narrative glitches).
Unnatural darkness spreads from the Temple at dusk—no mundane light can pierce it.

details: Vermin-Lord acolytes performing rituals with flesh-made instruments.
Sacrificed Unborn bound to trees, still aware, whispering.

encounters: Hollow Echo Beasts that steal voices.
Shrines that hum if touched—channel Atropus’ will.
A welcoming party of cultists who offer to guide the PCs to the Temple—but not back.
phases.effect: The jungle itself becomes a weapon. The party is in a place forgotten by gods but remembered by something else.

optional_mechanics: Rite of Silence: Players may attempt a holy rite or magical silence to mask their presence—limited uses.
Sacrificial Shortcut: A mad cultist may offer a faster path in exchange for something dear.
Mutated Jungle Pathways: Trails open or close depending on party behavior— if they burn something holy, the jungle lets them pass; if they speak the name of Sedna, the vines tighten.

fm.title: Stealth Preparation
fm.description: A complete tactical guide for preparing stealth operations in the jungles of Sedna. Covers gear modifications, scent masking, movement, campsite concealment, silent combat, psychological discipline, and final readiness checklists.
fm.overview: Strange Bones trains operatives to vanish into the jungle—seen only when they choose to strike. This guide details practical steps and mental conditioning to achieve near-perfect stealth through preparation, discipline, and environmental awareness.

sections.name: Gear Modifications for Maximum Stealth
sections.description: Techniques for reducing visibility, sound, and reflection through strategic alterations to clothing, armor, and weapons.

categories.title: Clothing & Armor Adjustments
items: Muted colors and camouflage using jungle moss, crushed berries, and charcoal.
Silencing metal gear: avoid chainmail or plate; wrap all metal parts in cloth or soft leather.
Padded footwear (moss or soft leather) to dampen footsteps.
Secure loose items—wrap rations and supplies in waxed cloth; use gourd containers instead of metal flasks.
Dull reflective surfaces with ash or charcoal; coat blades in blackened oil.
Favor bows, daggers, or bone knives over firearms or heavy melee weapons.

sections.name: Scent Masking & Suppression
sections.description: Predators smell before they see; masking scent is essential for survival in the deep jungle.

categories.title: Jungle Scent Techniques
items: Use crushed herbs, moss, or oils to cover scent; dust with damp earth or charcoal.
Avoid perfume, strong soap, and smoke; extinguish fires carefully to prevent soot smell.
Extreme measure: smear local animal blood to confuse predators and trackers.

sections.name: Movement & Travel Precautions
sections.description: Stealth in motion—how to travel unseen and unheard through dangerous terrain.

categories.title: Tactical Movement Adjustments
items: Move at half speed to gain advantage on Stealth checks.
Avoid dry leaves and twigs; step on moss or solid stone.
Use hand signals and pre-arranged gestures for communication.
Stay close to cover and shadows when advancing.
Plan movement during gusts or rainfall to mask sound.

sections.name: Campsite Stealth & Fire Discipline
sections.description: Proper rest practices for stealth missions; minimizing exposure while encamped.

categories.title: Safe Camping Procedures
items: No open flames; use buried embers or hot stones for heat.
Choose hidden campsites within dense vegetation or between fallen logs.
Scatter food scraps and bury waste far from camp.
Use false camps and decoy fires to mislead pursuers.

sections.name: Weapon & Combat Readiness for Silent Kills
sections.description: Combat should be fast, quiet, and decisive—noise is death.

categories.title: Silent Kill Tactics
items: Always strike from stealth to gain surprise.
Neutralize loud threats or casters first.
Use daggers, bows, and garrotes instead of firearms when possible.
Firearms: shoot from cover, then immediately relocate.
Employ hit-and-run tactics—strike, vanish, reappear elsewhere.
Use thrown objects or mimic jungle sounds to distract enemies.

sections.name: Psychological Warfare Against the Jungle’s Hunters
sections.description: The jungle whispers; its predators test resolve. Survival demands mental endurance.

categories.title: Mental Fortitude & Countermeasures
items: Never respond to the whispering fog or disembodied voices.
Carry fire but conceal it—predators fear light, yet fire attracts others.
Mark paths subtly using natural markers, not carvings or chalk symbols.
Do not stray from the group; those who walk alone in the western jungle do not return.

sections.name: Final Checklist Before Entering the Jungle
checklist: Armor and gear wrapped in cloth for silence.
Clothing camouflaged with mud and plant dyes.
Weapons and tools secured against clinking.
Scent masked with herbs, charcoal, and blood.
Supplies packed tightly to prevent rattling.
Final warning: The jungle watches. Do not leave tracks.

A secretive guild responsible for lighting and maintaining the city’s whale-oil lamps. They patrol the streets at night, carrying keys and oil, with whistles that serve as coded signals. Their reach gives them unmatched knowledge of the city after dark.

- Lamp patterns rumored to carry coded messages.

The Code is Black Brine’s brutal law of survival, enforced by the Council of Captains. Pirates live by it—or die by it.

# The Five Laws
1. **The Island Stays Secret** – Breakers are executed.  
2. **The Right to Keep What You Take** – Theft is legal until contested. Losers pay in flesh.

Little Sedna is a quiet, brooding corner of Black Brine built atop the moss-covered bones of a civilization long drowned. The district blends ancient stone ruins with humble modern dwellings, winding between weather-worn statues and half-sunken archways. It is a place of reverence, mystery, and forgotten power.

Narrow streets and stairways weave between old stone foundations and newer timber homes. The air is heavy with sea mist and incense.

nodes.body_excerpt:
# Overview
A converted chapel turned into a public library and meeting hall. The Library is one of the few places in Blackmire where learning, gossip, and records are freely exchanged. Its shelves mix genuine tomes with forgeries and cursed scrolls.

A desolate, bone-littered stretch of coastline on Sedna’s northeastern edge, Bleached Bones Beach is a graveyard of shipwrecks, leviathan carcasses, and cursed sailors. Narrow, between 50–70 feet wide, the beach stretches far north and south. To one side, jagged grey waves break violently; to the other, a sheer cliff rises with no clear path inland. Natural obstacles include the rotting skeleton of an ancient ship, broken masts, leviathan bones, and drift debris.

fm.name: Broadside Tavern
fm.overview: The Broadside Tavern is more than a watering hole—it is a gaming hall, ale house, and steamy bath house all in one. Known for its multilevel drinking hall and nightly performances, it draws pirates, nobles, informants, and adventurers alike into its orbit.
fm.geography: Located in the northern district of Little Sedna, the Broadside is accessible by main street and dockside. Its ancient interior features a gaming floor lined with well-worn tables where citizens gather to play games of chance, strategy, and skill. A high mezzanine overlooks the gaming floor for those who prefer music and drinking.
notable_features: The Mezzanine Stage: Hosts bards, illusionists, and playwrights. Performances often double as coded exchanges or fronts for clandestine dealings.
The Bath House: Fed by hot springs; a luxurious destination offering steaming baths, perfumed soaps, and restorative oils.
The Tideglass Bar: Renowned for rare spirits and fine liqueurs; its polished surface gleams like the midnight sea, reflecting faces with uncanny clarity.
Neutral Ground: Accepted as a political chessboard where pirate captains, council informants, and power brokers negotiate under a fragile veneer of discretion.
fm.demographics: Patrons vary nightly—pirates, merchants, nobles in disguise, foreign emissaries, and adventurers. Staff is small but skilled, led by Lira Vott and Baelin the Quiet.
fm.government_politics: The tavern operates as neutral ground, respected by rival gangs and factions. Agreements made here often carry weight across the city, enforced by the threat of collective retribution if neutrality is violated.
fm.economy: Profits flow from performances, exotic drinks, and fees for use of the bath house. Side income comes from debts, favors, and the information Lira Vott discreetly brokers.
fm.culture_daily_life: The Broadside is equal parts performance hall and game den. Nights blend revelry, danger, and whispered negotiations beneath layers of song, poetry, and stagecraft.

notable_npcs.name: Lira Vott
notable_npcs.description: Former bard, now tavern mistress. Witty, watchful, and a broker of secrets. Magical and financial debts keep her tethered to Black Brine’s intrigues.

notable_npcs.name: Baelin the Quiet
notable_npcs.description: Silent, precise, and ever-observant. Known for orchestrating the floor with subtle gestures, protecting patrons’ privacy.

adventure_hooks: A saboteur approaches the party in the Whisper Room, drawing them into political machinations.
Performances on the Gilded Stage conceal coded messages about an impending betrayal.
A missing guest may be trapped in the tavern’s shifting enchantments, hinting at a hidden passage or planar crossing.
Lira’s debts embroil the party in rivalries, assassination plots, or retrieval of cursed relics hidden under the Tideglass Bar.
campaign_connections: Rumors and job offers flow constantly—lost pirate ships, missing maps, and possible portals to the Underdark beneath the tavern floor.
Zhentarim, Harpers, and pirate crews use the Broadside as a maneuvering ground. Players may choose alliances or investigate disappearances linked to the Whisper Room.
The tavern is rumored to be built atop an ancient underwater temple. Prophecies foretell the return of a sea deity; storms and strange omens suggest its awakening.
secrets: The shifting decor is powered by a bound spirit—unhappy, but bound to Lira’s debts. Freeing or bargaining with it could reshape the tavern’s nature.
Beneath the Tideglass Bar lies a sealed hatch leading to catacombs that may connect to a temple of the Hollow Goddess.

nodes.name: Captain’s Club
nodes.body_excerpt:
# Overview
An invitation-only tavern built into the hull of an old warship, just off the main docks. It serves Black Brine’s elite—current and former ship captains, mercenary leaders, and smugglers. A half-sunken tavern propped on stilts above a stagnant canal. The Crooked Lantern is a haven for drunks, smugglers, and those seeking secrets whispered over cheap grog. Its warped beams and swaying lantern give it its name.  

# Notable Features
- Rumors traded more freely than coin.  
- Patrons vanish without explanation, feeding superstition.  
- Staff often found dazed, as if waking from dreams.

- A barkeep begs for help after a string of vanishings.  
- A dream-plagued NPC recounts visions of Sedna’s shrines.

- A relic trader offers a map fragment to Sedna’s shrines.

fm.name: Old Salt Eatery
fm.overview: A battered, half-sunken tavern perched on stilts above the Blackmire muck, the Old Salt Eatery is the district’s most reliable source of food, gossip, and cheap grog. It smells like burnt fish, spilled brine, and old secrets. Locals swear the soup tastes different every day—mostly because it does.
fm.geography: Located near the center of Blackmire, where the sludge channels narrow, the eatery hangs partially over a slow-moving canal. Lanterns strung on ropes sway in the fog, and planks creak with every footfall.
notable_features: Fish tank bar table filled with eels
Daily “Catch & Gamble” game where patrons bet on swamp creatures
Salt-crusted floorboards said to be blessed by Sedna (or cursed by the cook)
fm.demographics: Mostly Blackmire locals, laborers, smugglers, out-of-luck pirates, and the occasional Inquisitor.
fm.government_and_politics: Neutral ground—no blades drawn, no questions asked. Run by old sea dog Garrik “Salttooth” Vane, a retired cook with a hook for a hand and a tongue sharp as a filet knife.
fm.economy: Cheap meals, local brews, underground betting. Sometimes used for dead drops or hushed meetings in curtained corners.
fm.culture: Rowdy, reeking of brine and spice. Tables carved with old names and forgotten crews. Every night carries a different flavor of danger, but the regulars wouldn’t eat anywhere else.

notable_npcs.name: Garrik "Salttooth" Vane
notable_npcs.note: Claims to have cooked for three pirate kings; one-eyed; hook hand.

notable_npcs.name: Krixie
notable_npcs.note: Halfling with sticky fingers and a sharp memory.

notable_npcs.name: Branwell
notable_npcs.note: Off-duty dockhand who’s always there, always watching.

adventure_hooks: A regular customer was poisoned—accident, or message?
Vane has a map etched on a fishbone, but refuses to sell it.
Something is whispering through the eels in the bar tank…
secrets: The cellar opens into an old smuggler tunnel sealed for years.
Salttooth Vane once sailed with Bloodshot and knows more than he lets on.
The stew’s secret ingredient may be alchemically active—an accident or a weapon?
connected_locations: Whisperer’s Hollow (local legend tied to the menu)

fm.name: Powder Keg Tavern
fm.overview: Built against a sulfur-reeking cliffside, the Powder Keg Tavern is a den of debauchery, violence, and black-powder-fueled chaos. Frequent brawls, reckless drinking challenges, and the occasional explosion draw gunslingers, mercenaries, and smugglers seeking cheap rum and dangerous company.

notable_features.Main Hall: Dim, smoke-filled, crammed with rough-hewn tables and dented tankards.

notable_features.Cavern Brewery: Natural cavern behind the bar doubles as brewery and powder magazine; accidental blasts occur monthly.

notable_features.Cliffside Balcony: Precarious dueling ground and place to throw cheaters to the waves.

notable_features.Hidden Tunnel (Rumor): Supposedly leads to an old smuggler’s vault.

associated_npcs.name: Harlow "Blastcap" Grint
associated_npcs.notes: Ear lost to a cannon misfire; serves brews strong enough to floor an orc; uses smoke bombs to end fights.

associated_npcs.name: Penny "Quickhands" Locke
associated_npcs.notes: Former pickpocket; quick reflexes; keeps the city’s wanted list memorized.

associated_npcs.name: Slug
associated_npcs.notes: Ex-gunner; serves the Blunderbuss cocktail (lethal or divine); known for stabbing unruly patrons.

associated_npcs.name: Big Mags
associated_npcs.notes: Wears a butcher’s apron; Galleon’s Bounty stew has questionable “healing” power.

regulars.name: Captain Broome "The Twice-Hanged"
regulars.notes: Rope scars on neck; claims to have survived two hangings; drinks glowing green liquor; mutters about a cursed coin in Gallows Market.

regulars.name: Ettie "Firetongue" Jarr
regulars.notes: Alchemist and explosives dealer; perpetually singed; sells blasting sticks and powders; once burned down a ship and stole its treasure.

regulars.name: Duggan "The Walking Wreck"
regulars.notes: Survives nightly brawls; reputed to have taken a cannonball to the chest; undefeated in knockout bets.

adventure_hooks.A Black Powder Deal Gone Wrong: Someone stole powder from the back room; Blastcap needs it recovered fast.

adventure_hooks.The Smuggler’s Vault: A rumored tunnel beneath the tavern leads to treasure—if someone dares to brave it.

adventure_hooks.An Explosive Disappearance: Ettie vanishes after a failed experiment; her workshop smolders with clues.

nodes.body_excerpt:
# Overview
A cliff-hidden tower woven with demiplane seams, Rupert’s Rest is part fortress, part laboratory. It is both a refuge and prison for Rupert’s circle, wrapped in wards that shimmer at twilight.

- **Shifting Geometry:** Rooms realign themselves daily.  
- **Runed Gates:** Entrances open only to those with Rupert’s sigils.

nodes.name: The Bonewalk
nodes.body_excerpt:
# Overview
A narrow pier stitched from shipwreck timbers and whale bone. It groans like a dying hull when storms near, and lanterns along its spine gutter without wind.

# Notable Features
- Bone-pins and rib-arches carved with sailor prayers.
- Hidden mooring rings used by smugglers at low tide.
- Tide-pools that occasionally whisper back.

# Adventure Hooks
- At moonrise the Bonewalk keens; something comes in with the fog.
- A smuggler cache is wedged in a whale skull far below the tide line.
- A child goes missing; footprints end atop the pier’s last rib.

# Secrets (DM Only)
- The final pylon is driven through a drowned altar; it’s waking.
- Bone-carvings are a crude ward—removing them invites the sea in.

# Connected Locations
- **bb:district:crosswater**

# Scrip in Black Brine  
## Currency, Control, and Daily Life on Sedna

---

## What Is Scrip?

Scrip is the official currency of Black Brine—small, copper-based discs embossed with the Trade Authority seal and drilled with a hole so they can be strung together.

Each piece is:

- standardized  
- difficult to forge  
- easy to transport  
- widely recognized across Sedna  

Though it contains very little intrinsic value, scrip is the backbone of the island’s economy.

---

## Why Scrip Exists

Black Brine sits at the crossroads of piracy, privateering, and mercantile trade. Ships arrive carrying:

- gold  
- foreign coin  
- stolen treasure  
- unstable inflows of wealth  

If gold circulated freely, the local economy would collapse each time a pirate unloaded a fortune.

The Great Exchange Day is one of the most important civic events in Black Brine.

## Overview
The Trackless Sea is the broad expanse of ocean west of Faerûn, stretching beyond the Sword Coast and the Moonshae Isles into waters that few charts agree upon. It is named not for the absence of routes, but for their unreliability—currents shift, landmarks vanish beneath mist, and magical navigation often fails.

While coastal trade routes are well traveled, the deeper reaches of the Trackless Sea remain dangerous, isolating distant islands and fostering cultures cut off from mainland influence.

nodes.body_excerpt:
# Sedna Lore Poem

**

In the days when breath walked freely and the tides bowed to song, there came a voice not born of brine.

She rode upon winds unchained, with a laugh that bent the trees and eyes that stole worship from stone.

The people, once bent to the One Beneath, turned their faces skyward.

The drowning songs ceased. The deep altars lay dry. The temples opened to air, and incense climbed where blood once fell.

They called her the Shaper of the High Current,

The Sky-Blessed Flame,

The One Who Sings Without Chains.

But the Deep Mother does not forget. The Taker of Breath, She Who Waits Below—

She stirred in the silence left behind.

In a single tide without wave, the silence took shape. The sky was split. The earth wept salt.

Her vengeance fell not in rage, but in erasure.…

# Temple of Sedna

## Overview
Carved into the salt-bitten cliffs at the edge of Little Sedna, the Temple of Sedna is both sacred site and tidal tomb. Accessible only at low tide, its cavernous interior shifts between hushed sanctuary and flooded reliquary. Worshipers gather here in silence to honor the goddess of the deep, whose presence is said to rise and fall with the sea.

## Geography
The temple begins as a narrow fissure in the cliffside, opening into a vast oceanic cavern with natural columns and carved walkways. At high tide, the sea invades the temple, swallowing altars, pews, and pilgrims alike. At low tide, barnacle-covered stone floors are exposed, slick and shining in the dark.
